messages:

Subject: Initial Q: custom eviction windows & grace periods for PHI workloads

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday — the streaming latency numbers look promising. We have a couple procurement items to clear before moving to a POC: around data residency and post-termination data handling. Specifically: can Redwood support a bespoke "eviction" cadence for cached KV/state and a longer post-termination grace window during which we can request an expedited retrieval before deletion? Our security team needs the order form language to reflect this.

High level asks: 
- Ability to set per-account KV cache eviction window (e.g., 30 / 90 / 180 days)
- A configurable grace period after contract termination (30–90 days) where GridCare can request exports before irreversible deletion
- Clear SLA timings for irreversible wipe after the grace period, and an audit trail to show deletion occurred

Can you point to where these options live in the standard order form, and whether they require a bespoke addendum? Also attaching the security questionnaire sections that are blocking us.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Carter
Sr. Security Program Manager | GridCare Health

Subject: Re: Initial Q: custom eviction windows & grace periods for PHI workloads

Hi Emily — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Short answer: yes, we can support both per-account KV eviction windows and a post-termination retrieval/grace window, but the specifics (length, retention classification, export process) are captured in the Order Form & a short SLA addendum.

Quick summary of options:
- Eviction windows: configurable at order form time. Default: 30 days for KV cache; we can set 90/180 if you require. Note these are different from data retention for persistent storage (which is governed by custody/persistence clauses).
- Grace period after termination: we offer 30-day standard grace; 60–90 day windows are available as an add-on. During the grace window we hold backups in an exportable state; after that we run an irreversible wipe.
- Wipe SLA & audit: irreversible wipes are executed by our secure Erasure Service with verifiable logs; we can include a deletion certificate and a machine-readable audit manifest for compliance.

I attached a short draft clause we typically use and a retention matrix that maps object types to eviction vs. persistent retention. Neha — can you confirm which data classes require HSM-backed key escrow for GridCare (they noted PHI)? Karthik — can you prepare the exact order-form language we should propose for a 90-day grace window?

Next steps: I can loop in procurement if you'd like draft language in the next 48 hours and a trimmed order form addendum.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt

Emily

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Emily Carter <emily.carter@gridcare.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Sep 2026 11:10:00 -04:00
Subject: Proposed order-form language: GridCare bespoke eviction & grace window

Hi Emily / Paul — attaching a concise clause you can paste into your procurement system. I kept the language intentionally prescriptive to avoid back-and-forth redlines. Key points included: in-region erasure, export formats, audit manifest fields, and timing.

Suggested clause (text below for quick copy):
"Order Form Addendum — Data Eviction & Post-Termination Grace Window"
1) Eviction Window: Customer elects KV cache eviction window of 180 days (the "Eviction Window"). Eviction pertains only to transient KV/cache artifacts used to speed inference; it does not affect persistent customer data stored in dedicated persistence layers.
2) Post-Termination Grace Window: Upon contract termination, Redwood will retain exportable backups for a period of 90 calendar days (the "Grace Window"). During the Grace Window, Customer may request export of Customer Data in NDJSON or Parquet format. Redwood will fulfill export requests within 7 business days.
3) Irreversible Wipe: After the Grace Window, Redwood will perform an irreversible wipe of the Customer Data. Wipes will be executed in the same cloud region(s) where the data is held; Redwood will not transfer data cross-border for the purpose of erasure.
4) Deletion Certificate & Audit Manifest: Upon completion of an irreversible wipe, Redwood will provide a signed Deletion Certificate including: (a) list of data classes erased, (b) TTL and deletion timestamp, (c) cloud region(s) where the action occurred, and (d) a SHA-256 sink hash of the wipe job manifest.
5) Exceptions & Escrow: For PHI workloads requiring HSM-backed key escrow, Customer and Redwood will document key custody requirements in Appendix A; escrow or extended retention may be subject to additional fees.

Attachments: (1) Order-form-ready clause (text) and (2) Export cadence & format table.

If that looks ok I can produce a PDF addendum and a single-line order form field for Procurement to reference (e.g., "Eviction Window: 180 days — Grace Window: 90 days — Export SLA: 7 business days — In-region erase: yes").

— Karthik
Principal Product Counsel | Redwood Inference
